key_insight: A conservative finite element scheme for Kirchhoff-type equations achieves optimal spatial accuracy and second-order temporal accuracy, with exact discrete energy preservation for the homogeneous, constant-coefficient problem.
engineering_relevance: The method supports accurate simulation of nonlocal nonlinear wave models relevant to structural dynamics while preserving energy under specified conditions.
method: Conforming finite elements of arbitrary polynomial degree p in two spatial dimensions.
Picard iteration for the nonlinearity, with convergence analysis using discrete-Laplacian fractional-power norms.
evidence_signal: Manufactured-solution experiments reproduce second-order time convergence and spatial L² convergence of order h^(p+1), consistent with the proved error bounds.
watch_item: Exact discrete energy preservation is established only for the homogeneous, constant-coefficient problem and the exact solution of the discrete scheme; finite Picard tolerances may affect conservation.
paper_title: Conservative Finite Element Methods for Kirchhoff-Type Equations
